title: US power use to beat record highs in 2026 and 2027 as AI use surges, EIA says
source_used: Reuters lead paragraph (via TradingView page metadata) and bloomingbit relay of the EIA outlook; Digital Today relay checked
key_facts: The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) said in its Short-Term Energy Outlook on 6 Oct 2026 that US power consumption will hit records in 2026 and 2027.
Reuters (Scott DiSavino) attributes the rise to AI-hungry data centers and electrification.
Consumption is forecast to rise to 4,356 billion kWh in 2027 from a record 4,195 billion kWh in 2025 (bloomingbit gives the same figures as trillion kWh with three decimals).
Renewables are projected at 27% of generation by 2027; coal's share is forecast to fall to 15%.
AI and cryptocurrency data centers are named as drivers.
quote_evidence: US power consumption will rise to record highs in 2026 and 2027, driven by AI-hungry data centers and electrification, the US Energy Information Administration said in its Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) on Tuesday.
The agency said renewables' share of electricity generation is projected to climb to 27% by 2027, while coal's share is forecast to fall to 15%.
why_it_matters_hint: The official US forecast now puts AI data centers among the drivers of record electricity use.
notes: Reuters page returned 401. Read only Reuters' opening paragraph (TradingView metadata) and bloomingbit's short relay; the full Reuters text was not available. Digital Today's relay quotes 419.5 billion kWh for 2025, which is ten times too small against the other two; not used. Its extra price figures (wholesale +11%, PJM +41%) come via Cryptopolitan and were not verified, so left out.
